name: Bodyweight Squat
description: Trains the quadriceps, glutes and trunk stabilisers while building the fundamental sit-to-stand pattern used in daily life.
formCues: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned out slightly.
Initiate the movement by breaking at the hips and knees at the same time.
Keep the chest tall and the knees tracking over the toes.
Descend until the thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Drive through the whole foot and finish with the glutes squeezed.

name: Push-Up
description: Builds pressing strength through the chest, triceps and shoulders while training the trunk to hold a rigid plank.
formCues: Place the hands slightly wider than shoulder width with fingers spread.
Brace the core and squeeze the glutes so the body forms one straight line.
Lower the chest to within a fist of the floor with elbows at about 45 degrees.
Keep the neck neutral and the elbows from flaring straight out.
Press the floor away and finish with the shoulder blades spread at the top.

name: Jumping Jack
description: A rhythmic full-body jump that raises heart rate fast and warms up the hips, calves and shoulders together.
formCues: Start standing tall with feet together and arms at your sides.
Jump the feet out wide while sweeping the arms overhead in one smooth arc.
Land softly on the balls of the feet with a slight bend in the knees.
Keep the ribs down and avoid arching the lower back as the arms rise.
Return to the start position and settle into a steady breathing rhythm.

name: Forward Lunge
description: Trains each leg independently to correct side-to-side strength differences and improve single-leg stability.
formCues: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and hands on the hips.
Step forward far enough that both knees can reach 90 degrees.
Lower until the back knee hovers just above the floor.
Keep the front heel planted and the torso upright throughout.
Push back to the start through the front foot and alternate legs.

name: Glute Bridge
description: Activates the glutes and hamstrings while teaching the hips to extend without over-arching the lower back.
formCues: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart.
Press the lower back gently into the floor before you start.
Drive through the heels and lift the hips until knees, hips and shoulders align.
Squeeze the glutes hard at the top without arching the ribs.
Lower slowly under control and avoid resting on the floor between reps.

name: Forearm Plank
description: Develops isometric core endurance so the spine stays braced and stable under load and movement.
formCues: Set the elbows directly under the shoulders with forearms parallel.
Extend the legs and rest on the toes with feet hip-width apart.
Create a straight line from heels to head by bracing the abdominals.
Squeeze the glutes and tilt the pelvis slightly to protect the lower back.
Breathe steadily and keep the hips from rising or sagging.

name: Mountain Climber
description: Combines a hard shoulder brace with rapid hip flexion to lift heart rate while training anti-rotation core control.
formCues: Start in a high plank with wrists under shoulders and body in one line.
Brace the core so the hips stay level as the legs begin to move.
Drive one knee toward the chest without letting the foot touch down hard.
Switch legs in a controlled running rhythm rather than a frantic bounce.
Keep the shoulders stacked over the wrists and the head neutral.

name: Burpee
description: Challenges the entire body through a squat, plank and jump sequence to build conditioning and work capacity fast.
formCues: From standing, squat down and place both hands flat on the floor.
Jump the feet back to a plank and hold the hips level for a beat.
Perform one full push-up, keeping the elbows at 45 degrees.
Snap the feet back under the hips, then stand and drive overhead.
Finish with a small jump and land softly with bent knees.

name: High Knees
description: A running drill in place that spikes heart rate and trains hip flexor strength with quick, light ground contact.
formCues: Stand tall with the chest lifted and eyes forward.
Drive one knee up to hip height while staying on the balls of the feet.
Pump the arms in opposition with a short, sharp swing.
Keep the trunk tall instead of leaning back as the knee rises.
Land softly and immediately switch to the opposite leg.

name: Butt Kicks
description: A light cardiovascular drill that warms the hamstrings and sharpens the speed of the running leg recovery.
formCues: Stand tall with the feet under the hips and shoulders relaxed.
Jog in place while drawing the heel up toward the glute each stride.
Keep the knees pointing down rather than lifting in front.
Land quietly under the hips with a soft knee.
Swing the arms naturally and keep the breathing rhythmic.

name: Dead Bug
description: Teaches the core to resist extension while the limbs move, protecting the lower back during everyday reaching and lifting.
formCues: Lie on your back with arms reaching to the ceiling and hips at 90 degrees.
Flatten the lower back against the floor and keep it there.
Lower the right arm and left leg together toward the ground.
Stop before the lower back starts to lift and return to the start.
Repeat on the opposite side while exhaling on the reach.

name: Bird Dog
description: Trains spinal stability and balance by extending opposite limbs without letting the hips rotate or the back arch.
formCues: Set up on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Brace the abdominals to keep the back flat and level.
Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are horizontal.
Keep the hips square to the floor and avoid rotating through the pelvis.
Pause briefly, return with control and alternate sides.

name: Superman Hold
description: Strengthens the spinal erectors, glutes and rear shoulders to counterbalance long hours of seated posture.
formCues: Lie face down with the arms extended overhead and legs straight.
Set the gaze at the floor to keep the neck in a neutral line.
Lift the chest, arms and thighs a few centimetres off the ground.
Squeeze the glutes and mid-back rather than cranking the neck up.
Hold for a count, then lower slowly without dropping the limbs.

name: Side Plank
description: Builds oblique and lateral hip strength so the trunk resists side bending during running, carrying and lifting.
formCues: Lie on your side with the elbow directly beneath the shoulder.
Stack or slightly stagger the feet for a stable base.
Lift the hips until the body forms a straight line from ankle to head.
Push the bottom shoulder away from the floor to avoid sinking.
Hold the position while breathing steadily and keep the hips high.

name: Standing Calf Raise
description: Strengthens the calves and ankle complex for safer jumping, stable landings and better running push-off.
formCues: Stand tall with the feet hip-width apart near a wall for balance.
Keep the weight over the balls of the feet throughout the set.
Rise as high as possible onto the toes with a controlled tempo.
Pause at the top and avoid rolling the ankles outward.
Lower slowly until the heels reach the floor and repeat.

name: Wall Sit
description: An isometric hold that builds endurance and mental toughness in the quadriceps without stressing the knees.
formCues: Place the whole back flat against a wall and step the feet out.
Slide down until the knees sit at roughly 90 degrees.
Keep the knees stacked over the ankles and pointing forward.
Press the lower back into the wall and rest the hands on the thighs.
Hold steady while breathing and avoid resting the weight on the hands.

name: Chair Dip
description: Isolates the triceps and strengthens the shoulders through a controlled bodyweight pressing range.
formCues: Sit on the edge of a sturdy chair and grip it with both hands.
Slide the hips forward off the seat with legs extended or bent.
Keep the chest tall and the shoulders pulled away from the ears.
Bend the elbows straight back and lower until the upper arms are parallel.
Press through the palms to lock out without shrugging at the top.

name: Knee Push-Up
description: A regressed pressing pattern that lets beginners build the chest and triceps strength needed for full push-ups.
formCues: Kneel with the hands placed slightly wider than the shoulders.
Walk the hands out so the body forms a straight line from head to knees.
Brace the core and keep the glutes engaged to prevent a hip hinge.
Lower the chest under control until it is a hand from the floor.
Press back up fully and keep the elbows from flaring wide.

name: Incline Push-Up
description: Reduces the load on a raised surface so beginners can practise full-range pressing with correct body alignment.
formCues: Place the hands on a stable raised surface such as a table edge.
Walk the feet back until the body forms one rigid diagonal line.
Keep the elbows angled back rather than flared to the sides.
Lower the chest to the edge while bracing the abdominals.
Push away from the surface and fully extend the arms at the top.

name: Pike Push-Up
description: Shifts the pressing load onto the shoulders and upper chest to prepare for harder overhead strength work.
formCues: Start in a plank, then walk the feet in and lift the hips high.
Keep the legs straight and form an inverted V with the body.
Set the hands shoulder-width apart with the head between the arms.
Bend the elbows and lower the crown of the head toward the floor.
Press back to the start and keep the hips lifted throughout.

name: Inchworm
description: Combines hamstring mobility, shoulder stability and core control in one flowing full-body movement.
formCues: Stand tall, then hinge forward and place the hands on the floor.
Walk the hands out until the body reaches a strong plank position.
Pause for one second with the core braced and hips level.
Walk the feet toward the hands with the knees as straight as possible.
Roll up through the spine one vertebra at a time to stand.

name: Skater Jump
description: A lateral bound that develops side-to-side power, balance and conditioning for sport and daily agility.
formCues: Start standing tall with the weight on the right leg.
Push off laterally and land softly on the opposite foot.
Let the trailing leg swing behind for balance without touching down.
Keep the chest lifted and the knee aligned over the landing foot.
Bound back and forth with quiet, controlled landings.

name: Sumo Squat
description: A wide-stance squat that targets the inner thighs and glutes while demanding strong hip opening.
formCues: Take a wide stance with the toes turned out about 30 degrees.
Keep the chest tall and the shoulders stacked over the hips.
Sit straight down between the heels rather than shifting forward.
Lower until the thighs are parallel while the knees track over the toes.
Push the floor apart through the heels and squeeze the glutes to stand.

name: Bodyweight Good Morning
description: A hip hinge that loads the hamstrings and lower back safely, teaching the pattern behind every deadlift variation.
formCues: Stand with the feet hip-width apart and hands behind the head.
Soften the knees and brace the abdominals before hinging.
Push the hips straight back while the chest leads forward.
Lower until the torso is near parallel with a flat spine.
Drive the hips forward to stand tall and finish with the glutes.

name: Elevated Hip Thrust
description: Uses a chair edge to increase hip range and place maximum tension on the glutes through full extension.
formCues: Rest the upper back on the edge of a sturdy chair or sofa.
Plant the feet hip-width apart so the shins are vertical at the top.
Tuck the chin slightly and brace the ribs down.
Drive through the heels until the hips are fully extended.
Hold the squeeze for one second and lower without losing tension.

name: Cossack Squat
description: Develops deep hip mobility and single-leg strength through a wide lateral squat pattern.
formCues: Stand with the feet much wider than shoulder width and toes out.
Shift the weight to one side and bend that knee deeply.
Keep the opposite leg straight with the heel on the floor and toes up.
Stay tall through the chest and sink as low as mobility allows.
Push back through the loaded heel and repeat on the other side.

name: Bicycle Crunch
description: Trains the rectus abdominis and obliques together through a controlled rotational crunch pattern.
formCues: Lie on your back with the fingertips lightly behind the ears.
Lift the shoulder blades and bring both knees to 90 degrees.
Rotate the torso so one elbow travels toward the opposite knee.
Extend the other leg long without letting it touch the floor.
Move smoothly and avoid pulling on the neck during the twist.

name: Lying Leg Raise
description: Strengthens the lower abdominals and hip flexors while teaching the pelvis to stay stable under a long lever.
formCues: Lie flat with the legs straight and hands beside the hips.
Press the lower back into the floor before lifting the legs.
Raise both legs to vertical while keeping the knees locked.
Lower slowly and stop just before the heels touch the ground.
Exhale on the lift and avoid arching the back on the descent.

name: Russian Twist
description: Builds rotational core strength and oblique control that carry over to throwing, turning and lifting tasks.
formCues: Sit with the knees bent and lean back until the torso is at 45 degrees.
Lift the feet lightly off the floor for an advanced base.
Clasp the hands and rotate from the ribcage, not just the arms.
Turn fully to one side, then the other, keeping the hips still.
Keep the chest tall and the breathing continuous through each twist.

name: V-Up
description: A demanding full-range abdominal movement that folds the torso and legs together for maximum core tension.
formCues: Lie flat with the arms extended overhead and legs straight.
Brace hard and lift the legs and torso at the same time.
Reach the hands toward the toes and balance on the sit bones.
Keep the spine long rather than rounding heavily through the shoulders.
Lower both halves under control and stop before resting fully.

name: Flutter Kick
description: Sustained low-range kicks that build endurance in the lower abdominals while keeping the back stable.
formCues: Lie on your back with the hands placed under the lower back.
Lift both heels a few centimetres off the floor.
Kick the legs up and down in small, quick alternating strokes.
Keep the lower back pressed into the floor throughout.
Point the toes and keep the movement from the hips, not the knees.

name: Cat-Cow
description: Mobilises the spine segment by segment and relieves stiffness from prolonged sitting or sleeping.
formCues: Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Inhale and drop the belly while lifting the chest and tailbone.
Exhale and round the spine toward the ceiling, tucking the chin.
Move slowly and let each vertebra participate in the curve.
Match one full breath to each direction of the movement.

name: World's Greatest Stretch
description: Combines hip, hamstring, groin and thoracic mobility in a single flowing pattern for a complete warm-up.
formCues: Step into a long lunge and place both hands inside the front foot.
Sink the hips forward while keeping the back leg straight and active.
Drop the inside elbow toward the floor to deepen the hip stretch.
Rotate the top arm to the ceiling and follow it with your gaze.
Return to the start and repeat on the opposite side.

name: Thoracic Rotation
description: Restores upper-back rotation so the shoulders and neck can move freely without compensation from the lower back.
formCues: Kneel on all fours and place one hand behind the head.
Keep the hips square and the opposite arm firmly planted.
Rotate the elbow down toward the opposite wrist to start.
Open the chest and point the elbow to the ceiling in a smooth arc.
Pause at the top and repeat before switching sides.

name: Towel Shoulder Dislocates
description: Uses a towel to guide the shoulders through full range, improving overhead mobility for pressing and reaching.
formCues: Hold a towel with both hands much wider than shoulder width.
Stand tall with the ribs down and the knees softly bent.
Raise the arms overhead with straight elbows in a wide arc.
Take the towel back behind the hips as far as control allows.
Reverse the path to the front and narrow the grip only when it feels easy.

name: Warrior Flow
description: Links Warrior I and Warrior II poses to open the hips and shoulders while building quiet lower-body endurance.
formCues: Step into a long stance with the front knee stacked over the ankle.
Turn the back foot out slightly and press the outer edge down.
Sink into the front hip while keeping the torso tall and stacked.
Extend the arms with the shoulders relaxed away from the ears.
Breathe slowly and switch sides after the hold with equal control.

name: Downward Dog
description: Stretches the hamstrings and calves while training the shoulders to support body weight in an inverted position.
formCues: From all fours, lift the hips high and straighten the arms.
Spread the fingers wide and press evenly through the palms.
Push the floor away so the chest moves toward the thighs.
Let the heels reach toward the floor with the knees softly bent.
Hold long, slow breaths and keep the head between the arms.

name: Cobra Stretch
description: Gently extends the spine and opens the chest to counter the rounded posture created by desk and phone use.
formCues: Lie face down with the palms under the shoulders and elbows tucked.
Set the legs long with the tops of the feet resting on the floor.
Press lightly into the hands and lift the chest a comfortable height.
Draw the shoulders back and down away from the ears.
Keep the hips grounded and breathe into the front of the body.

name: Child's Pose
description: A restorative resting position that releases the lower back, hips and shoulders between demanding efforts.
formCues: Kneel with the big toes together and the knees comfortably wide.
Sit the hips back toward the heels and fold the torso forward.
Walk the fingertips forward to lengthen through the sides.
Rest the forehead on the floor or a folded towel.
Breathe deeply into the back of the ribs and soften the shoulders.

name: Bear Crawl In Place
description: A low crawling pattern that builds shoulder stability, coordination and total-body conditioning without equipment.
formCues: Start on all fours and lift the knees one inch off the ground.
Keep the back flat enough to balance a water bottle on the lower back.
Move the opposite hand and foot forward together in small steps.
Stay low through the hips and keep the knees near the floor.
Alternate directions within your space and keep the breathing steady.
